question: Can an automated system build reusable physical concepts from noisy data across many experiments and use them to discover increasingly general laws without seeding domain-specific physics?

key_findings.claim: AI-Newton represents measurements, intrinsic properties, experiment-specific relations, and general laws in an explicit physical domain-specific language rather than in latent neural features.
key_findings.evidence: The theory base separates symbols, concepts, and laws. Newly defined concepts retain the experiment that measures them, allowing values such as mass to be recalled consistently across later problems and reused in concise candidate laws.

key_findings.claim: The discovery loop proposes specific laws, simplifies them symbolically, analyzes controlled-variable dependencies, and promotes reusable expressions into concepts and broader laws through plausible reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Trials select experiments and available concepts, search expressions, simplify differential-algebraic relations with a Rosenfeld-Groebner procedure, classify dependencies, and extract conserved or repeated quantities as new concepts. An era-control policy expands the search only after sufficient progress.

key_findings.claim: Across ten noisy simulated-mechanics runs, the prototype reconstructs a coherent chain including mass, force, Newton's second law, kinetic and potential energies, energy conservation, and universal gravitation.
key_findings.evidence: With up to 1,200 trials and an average 48-hour run, the system reports about 90 concepts and 50 general laws on average. Discovery timing varies across runs but tends to progress from simpler concepts such as mass to force and energy laws that cover the experiment collection.

key_findings.claim: The phrase 'without prior physical knowledge' is narrower than complete tabula rasa because the system embeds a symbolic language, algebraic operators, simplification routines, plausible-reasoning rules, and a curated experiment suite.
key_findings.evidence: No named physical quantities beyond spacetime are seeded, but the workflow and DSL specify what expressions, dependency tests, and generalization moves can be searched. This is a reviewer interpretation of the engineered discovery prior, not a contradiction of the paper's narrower claim about unseeded physical concepts and laws.

method.core_idea: Accumulate an explicit hierarchy of symbols, measurable concepts, specific laws, and general laws across a curriculum of simulated experiments.
method.mechanism: Each trial selects an experiment and known concepts, searches symbolic relations, simplifies them, tests their object and parameter dependencies, and uses plausible-reasoning templates to define new measurable concepts or generalize recurring laws. The growing theory base changes the representation and compresses later searches.
assumptions: Observed dynamics can be expressed with the provided algebraic and differential DSL.
The experiment collection varies relevant factors enough to distinguish intrinsic properties and general laws.
Noise and numerical fitting do not make symbolic equivalence and dependency tests unreliable.
The hand-designed plausible-reasoning rules capture useful scientific abstraction moves.

techniques.role: Promotes reusable measured quantities into explicit symbolic concepts.
Searches and generalizes equations using evidence from multiple experimental configurations.
Compresses discovered relations before dependency classification and reuse.

evaluations.setting: Ten runs over a noisy simulated Newtonian-mechanics experiment suite
evaluations.metric: concepts and general laws recovered plus discovery timing
evaluations.result: At most 1,200 trials and about 48 hours per run, the system reports roughly 90 concepts and 50 general laws on average, including Newton's second law, energy conservation, and universal gravitation.
evaluations.baseline: Known target physics and repeated stochastic runs; no head-to-head compute-normalized symbolic-regression baseline is reported in the main paper.

limitations: The demonstration is confined to simulated classical mechanics and a restricted symbolic language.
The main evaluation checks rediscovery of known laws rather than prospective discovery on held-out unknown systems.
No compute-matched ablation isolates the value of concept promotion, plausible reasoning, era control, and algebraic simplification.
Reviewer inference: engineered representational and reasoning priors are substantial even though physical concepts and named laws are not preloaded.
failure_modes: The DSL cannot express the governing law or requires a prohibitively large symbolic search.
Correlated experiments cause spurious quantities to appear intrinsic or general.
Noise makes equivalent concepts look different, fragmenting the theory base.
A wrongly promoted concept constrains later search and creates a self-consistent but false theory.
reusable_insights: Scientific-discovery systems can reduce later search by retaining how abstract quantities are operationally measured.
Cross-experiment invariance is a stronger signal of a physical concept than fit quality on one dataset.
A discovery system should expose its symbolic and reasoning priors when claiming autonomy.
open_questions: Does the hierarchy recover useful abstractions when the true law is outside the original DSL?
How should false concepts be revised or removed when later experiments contradict them?
Can the system design information-gaining experiments rather than consume a curated fixed suite?
How does it compare to modern symbolic-regression and LLM scientist agents under equal computation?

competitive_landscape.title: AI Feynman: A physics-inspired method for symbolic regression
competitive_landscape.difference: AI Feynman applies physics-inspired separability and symmetry tests to recover a formula from a dataset. AI-Newton accumulates explicitly measurable concepts and generalizes laws across an experiment collection, but embeds a broader hand-designed discovery workflow.

competitive_landscape.title: AI Feynman 2.0: Pareto-optimal symbolic regression exploiting graph modularity
competitive_landscape.difference: AI Feynman 2.0 targets Pareto-optimal accuracy-complexity formulas and modular structure for individual regression problems. AI-Newton's search is organized around reusable cross-problem concepts and theory-base growth rather than a single equation frontier.

competitive_landscape.title: Rediscovering orbital mechanics with machine learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Cranmer et al. encode translational and rotational equivariance plus Newtonian interaction assumptions in a graph simulator and use symbolic regression to recover gravitation. AI-Newton aims to infer quantities such as mass and force from a broader experiment suite without seeding those particular physics assumptions.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Symbolic Regression: Recovering Mathematical Expressions from Data via Risk-Seeking Policy Gradients
competitive_landscape.difference: Deep Symbolic Regression learns a distribution over expression trees and optimizes high-reward formulas end to end. AI-Newton uses explicit concepts, deterministic algebraic simplification, and cross-experiment plausible reasoning to restructure the search over time.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after comparison: AI-Newton's strongest novelty is persistent, operationally grounded concept formation across experiments and progressive law generalization, not raw symbolic-regression accuracy. The mechanics rediscovery establishes an integrated proof of concept; stronger claims require ablations and prospective domains where the target abstraction is not already known.
reviewer_notes: The six-page primary text and its dense workflow, evaluation, figures, and references were reviewed. The paper itself points to supplementary materials for implementation details not present in the indexed PDF, which limits audit depth. Competitor records were checked at primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
